sentences.text:
Counsel for Applicant :- Shamshad Ahmad,Varsha Singh Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Samit Gopal,J.
1. List revised.

2. Heard Ms. Varsha Singh, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri B.B. Upadhyay, learned counsel for the State and perused the record.
3.

This application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. has been filed by the applicant Shweta Gond with the prayer to direct the learned Special Chief Judicial Magistrate, Varanasi in Complaint Case No. 878 of 2019, Shweta Gond vs. Sandeep Kumar and others, u/s 498A, 594, 506 I.P.C., P.S. Rohaniya,
District Varanasi pending in the court of Special Chief Judicial Magistrate, Varanasi within stipulated period.

entities.text: Shweta Gond vs. Sandeep Kumar and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Shweta Gond vs State Of U.P. And 6 Others on 17 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149285199/
1 4.

entities.text: Shweta Gond vs State Of U.P. And 6 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant argued that the trial is of the year 2019.

It is argued that delay in disposal of the said case is causing irreparable loss and hardship to the applicant and as such appropriate direction be issued for disposal of trial in time bound manner.
5.

Per contra, learned State counsel opposed the prayer made in the present matter by arguing that no such specific reasons have been made out for giving any direction for expediting the trial of the case and as such the application be dismissed.
6. After having heard learned counsels for the parties and perusing the record, it is evident that the trial is of the year 2019.
The same as per order sheet is going on.
There is no specific reason for expediting the same.

However, the applicant who is complainant of the case, may file an application for expediting the trial of the case before the court concerned within two weeks from today, which may as per its load of work, diary and pendency of cases, pass appropriate orders on the same within two weeks thereafter.
7. It is made clear that this Court has not passed any direction for expediting the trial.
8. The present application is disposed of.
